chunks.content: 96 Make This Your Last Miserable Tax Season Ever Sara, It’s the day before the deadline and in the last few weeks I’ve been getting A LOT of emails and calls from former clients saying ‘I’m never doing this again, find me a buyer or I’m burning it down’ If the thought of one more tax season makes you want to lock the door and throw your laptop in the ocean… you’re not alone. Here’s the good news: You’ve got options. Whether you want to offload your firm completely or just lighten your load, now’s the time to act—not mid-February when you’re buried in 1099s and caffeine. I know you’re tired and you simply cannot add on, but save this email for next week because May is the perfect time to make sure you do not do this to yourself yet again. Here’s your “get-out-of-misery” menu: 1. Sell Your Firm and Walk Away If you’re done-done—burned out, over it, and ready for the next chapter—you can sell 100% of your firm and exit entirely. With the right buyer and a clean transition plan, you’ll likely get paid for what you’ve built and never have to file another extension (except your own from your sailboat) 2. Sell Your Firm and Stay On (Without the Stress) Hand off ownership, keep your favorite clients, and show up like a normal employee—minus the late nights, payroll stress, or management headaches. Many buyers offer rollover equity, letting you cash out partially now and still benefit from future growth or resale. 3. Sell a Majority, Keep a Minority Stake This is the "have your cake and eat it too" option. Sell a majority stake to a partner who takes over operations, while you keep a seat at the table (and some future upside). Can be perfect if you still love the work but not the grind of running the firm. 4. Merge with a Larger Firm (and Sell into It) Join forces with a larger, better-resourced firm. You sell your book into theirs, get support with staffing and tech, and possibly take a leadership or client service role post-merger. This often comes with equity or bonus payouts tied to performance. 5. Sell Internally with SBA-Backed Financing Let a trusted employee or junior partner buy you out over time using SBA financing. You’ll phase out at your pace while mentoring the next generation. Bonus: you can structure this to get your full value and a smoother transition for clients. 6. Package Your Firm for a Search Fund Buyer There’s a growing pool of motivated buyers—often MBAs with investor backing—who are looking to buy and run firms just like yours. You sell, help them get up to speed for a few months, and then hand over the reins while keeping some seller financing or equity in the deal. If even one of those options sounds like something you need to do, don’t wait until you’re staring down the barrel of another tax season... reply to this email and let’s make a plan. To a smooth tax season, Sara Sharp Partner, SK&S Law Group Business Consultant & Founder of Deal Academy P.S.
